Definition: to secrete, by act or word; hence (intensively) to destroy
BiblicalUsage: Kachad is hiding — to keep a thing back by act or by word, and sometimes to destroy it by hiding it away. The Egyptians tell Joseph they cannot hide their poverty from him; God promises to cut off the nations before Israel; and David says he has not hid God's righteousness within his heart but has declared it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe hiding is the first instinct of sin and the last thing faith does. Adam hid, David declared — and I have learned that what I hide grows in the dark, while what I confess to God loses its power.
